problems.stem: Your four-person group needs to edit one shared report. Which sharing setting fits the task?
options: Anyone with the link can edit
Share to the four named teammates as editors; anyone else gets view-only or no access
Make it fully public on the web
Email a copy to each person so there are four versions
problems.explanation: Give the team the least access they need. Public edit invites strangers; four separate copies fragment the work.

problems.stem: You disagree with a teammate's paragraph in a shared doc. What keeps the change visible and reversible?
options: Delete it and retype your version
Use Suggesting mode or a comment so the teammate can see and accept or reject the change
Rewrite it overnight without telling anyone
Lock them out of the document
problems.explanation: Suggestions and comments preserve the original and show what changed, instead of silently overwriting a teammate.

problems.stem: Two teammates keep retyping the same intro at the same time and edits get lost. What norm prevents this?
options: Everyone edits everything whenever they want
Assign section owners (you: intro, me: methods) so people do not collide on the same text
Make the document read-only for everyone
problems.explanation: Dividing ownership stops two people writing over each other in the same paragraph.

problems.stem: The group report is due Friday 11:59 PM. The last section keeps arriving at 11:55 PM with no time to check it. What norm fixes this?
options: Set an internal deadline 24 hours before the real one so the team can review and fix before submitting
problems.explanation: An earlier internal deadline builds in review time so the whole group is not gambling at 11:55 PM.
